reviews.title: 6.9mm/H²0? I believe it.
reviews.comment: Coming from someone who ended up being disassapointed with the base P12s: Despite acknowledging their position on the value throne. I found them unusable due to what I suppose is an acoustic sensitivity to resonance harmonics those fans were brutally prone to. P12 Pros? Acoustically level. Constant. And with that being the only gripe I *had, now I have nothing but praise to give. First and foremost. The exceptionally high static pressure rating isn't unfounded. My application that needed fans like these come from my DIY air purifier. Where the fans need to pull through 2 stacks of Merv 13 and Merv 4 equivalent carbon filters. This is a very high resistance environment and the P12 Pros massively outperform NF P12 Redux's in pulling dusty air which can be visualized with a bright flashlight. Part of this is obvious. It's a 3000rpm fan. But when normalizing for (anecdotal, and not measured) perceived noise, the P12 Pros are far less impeded by the air purifier filters. There are far too many reviews stating these are loud. Here's my, "impression" of it's actual noise. At max speed, they certainly sound like 3000rpm fan. A higher pitched hum for sure. However this is not a "loud" noise (think of how loud something is from an adjacent room or behind a closed door). This "loudness" is comparable if not quieter than most fans at 1700rpm and lower (which is around 55% PWM) They do make an audible "motor growl" when starting from 0rpm, which may be a nuisance to people who prefer fan curves that drop to 0. All in all. For my use case? A continuous operation high resistance environment? This is truly a remarkable fan especially for it's value. As a PC fan, I can't say. But I can speculate these fans are far more "fan" than most consumer hobbyist PC builds would need. And hard to justify with the quirks that come with being, 3000rpm brings. Acoustically anyway. Thank you Arctic.

reviews.title: cost effective
reviews.comment: for some reason my 3 intake fans are louder than the 2 exhausts. im not sure if it's because of fixing the screws too much or rpm resonance or restrictive space (small physical space with dust filter). the intakes have this very noticable high pitch droning sound starting from 1100+rpm. all 5 fans rev up noise is quite noticable (droning sound like it's going up to 1200rpm very shortly and going back to the set speed, using FanControl, this occurs at most speed level, I've even made sure the bios is set to pwm so I'm not sure what happened). despite all that I'd say this is a pretty good deal, not everyone can afford to get noctuas. they are cheap fans and they work well, just need to tune the curve a bit.
